maria: quick smoke results from the TF-tiling experiment across regions. ran reranker embed (sbert-like) with dims=256/512, batch sizes 1/8/32, backend=flash-tile + fallback to matmul. sending raw notes.

sam: nice — top-level numbers?

maria: eu-west G5 (NVLink) — dims=512 b=8: throughput ~620 qps, p95=42ms. us-west G5 same config ~640 qps p95=39ms. ap-south G4 (PCIe) ~290 qps p95=110ms (NUMA effects).

alex: cpu baseline?

maria: c6g.large (ARM) dims=256 b=32: ~120 qps, p95=230ms. surprising: for dims=256 b=1, CPU latency p95=45ms — good single-thread matmul path.

jen: any quant/INT8 runs?

maria: ran int8 auto-quant on 512 model — throughput +28% on G5 but p95 regressed by ~6ms occasionally (tail from dequant). quality check looks ok on eval set but need more coverage.

sam: can you paste the exact command you used?

maria: ```
# quick runner
bench_runner --model sbert_512 --dims 512 --batch 8 --backend flash-tile --quant int8 --region eu-west --cpu_fallback on
```

alex: thanks. two followups: (1) try flash-tile with smaller tile size (64 -> 32) to see p95 tail, (2) run same runs in us-east to validate region variance.

maria: queued both. also noticed proxying increased tail in ap-south when cross-region fetch enabled — likely PCIe + network + cold NVMe paging.

jen: pinging @infra-bot for kernel build with tile-size override and NUMA-aware affinity (set numa_policy=preferred).

infra-bot: build triggered: jenkins/job/tiling-kernel/2053456798 — will post artifact and perf job link once done :gear:
